content:
You’re doing a solid job settling into Warrior I. Let’s make a few adjustments so the pose feels stronger and more supported.

First, straighten your spine. Right now, your spine is not straight, so think about lifting up through the crown of your head and lengthening evenly through your torso. Try to avoid collapsing or leaning, and instead create one long, upright line through your upper body.

Next, bring your arms straight up. Your arms are not straight up at the moment, so reach them actively toward the ceiling. Keep that upward energy through your fingertips and let both arms extend fully so the pose feels more lifted and intentional.

Also, check your front leg alignment. Your knee is not directly over your ankle, and that’s an important adjustment for stability and support. Shift gently so that your front knee stacks directly over your ankle, creating a stronger foundation in the pose.

You’re very close—just focus on a straight spine, arms reaching straight up, and your knee directly over your ankle. Keep breathing steadily, and the pose will feel much more balanced and powerful.
